title: The Afternoon Brief: Roster churn and resignation calls define a busy Tuesday
dek: The Angels overhauled their pitching staff, transfer business moved fast in England and Italy, and a former FIFA Council member broke ranks to call for Infantino's resignation.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: The day's clearest thread is organizations making visible changes under pressure, from a last-place pitching staff to a FIFA governance rift, while several injury and investigation stories remain open and unresolved.
bottom_line: Tuesday's theme was institutions and individuals making visible moves under pressure: the Angels dismissed their entire pitching coaching staff amid a last-place, 45-74 season, Barcelona lost forward Roony Bardghji to a second ACL tear in the same knee, and former FIFA Council member Isha Johansen became the first prominent African football figure to publicly call for Gianni Infantino's resignation. Transfer business also moved briskly, with Fulham, Nottingham Forest, Manchester City, and Inter Milan all involved in completed or advancing deals. The evidence supports what happened in each case but leaves open questions unresolved, including Bardghji's recovery timeline, the intent behind Carrington's social media post, and whether other African officials will follow Johansen. Watch for updates on Jonathan Greenard's and Qwan'tez Stiggers's injury status, HISA's findings on the Saratoga and Monmouth Park races, and whether the Spence-to-Inter talks conclude.
body: The single thread running through Tuesday is institutions reacting to pressure in real time. The Angels fired their entire pitching coaching staff mid-season, Barcelona lost a young forward to a recurring injury that closes off his transfer options, and a former FIFA Council member broke from continental consensus to call publicly for Gianni Infantino's resignation. Each story is an organization or individual responding to a strain that had been building.

In baseball, the Angels dismissed pitching coach Mike Maddux, assistant pitching coach Darryl Scott, and bullpen coach Dom Chiti on Tuesday, with Tim Leveque and Michael Wuertz stepping in as interim replacements. The team sits at 45-74, the worst record in MLB, and is on pace for an 11th consecutive losing season. The pitching staff carries a 4.51 ERA, seventh-worst in the majors, and leads all of baseball in walks with 508 through Monday's games. The move gives the interim staff roughly seven weeks to show something different.

European soccer's transfer window kept moving on several fronts. Fulham completed a deal for midfielder Shea Charles from Southampton, reported at £30m, making him the most expensive Northern Ireland footballer ever on a five-year contract. Nottingham Forest signed Ivory Coast defender Ousmane Diomande from Sporting CP for a reported £34m on a four-year deal with a one-year option. Manchester City brought in goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli from Marseille on a two-year deal to back up Gianluigi Donnarumma, filling the gap left by James Trafford's move to Leeds. Inter Milan remain in advanced, unfinished talks with Tottenham over full-back Djed Spence, valued at a minimum of £25.6m. Meanwhile Barcelona forward Roony Bardghji tore the ACL in his right knee in training, the second tear to the same knee in two years, ruling him out of any summer move before the September 1 deadline and sidelining him for months.

Injury and medical news carried through the NFL as well. Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard, signed to a four-year, $100 million extension, will miss at least another couple of weeks with a pectoral strain, and cast doubt on whether Greenard practices before the regular season. Jets cornerback Qwan'tez Stiggers collapsed during a joint practice with Tampa Bay, was given an IV on the field, and was taken by ambulance to a hospital for evaluation; coach Aaron Glenn said he was conscious and able to speak, though the diagnosis and return timeline are not yet known. Separately, former NFL quarterback Matt Hasselbeck underwent brain scans, blood tests, and cognitive assessments at Boston University as part of a multi-site, NIH-funded effort to find the first method of diagnosing CTE in a living patient, a disease confirmed in more than 100 former NFL players only after death.

In basketball, Chicago's DiJonai Carrington responded to criticism of a social media post made after her ejection from a Sky-Fever game for a hard foul on Sophie Cunningham. She wrote on X that she never claimed the foul assessment itself was based on white privilege, pushing back on criticism from Emmanuel Acho and Cunningham. What she intended by tagging the Fever in the original post is not addressed in the reporting, and the dispute over that intent remains open.

On the business and governance side, Comcast and Disney ended a three-month carriage dispute, restoring NFL Network and NFL RedZone to Comcast platforms after the channels went dark in late April; financial terms were not disclosed. In FIFA's governance fight, former Council member Isha Johansen publicly called on Infantino to resign over the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal, becoming the first prominent African football figure to break from the continental bloc that has backed him. Johansen invoked Infantino's own 2021 advice to her to step down for the good of football. CAF's executive committee has unanimously backed his 2027 re-election, and whether other African officials follow her remains unreported.

Also Tuesday, HISA opened an investigation into five races held Sunday at Saratoga and Monmouth Park after U.S. and U.K. bookmakers flagged unusual betting patterns on horses linked to the same Maryland training facility; four of the five horses won despite long layoffs and weak prior form. And at the European Athletics Championships, Jakob Ingebrigtsen won 5,000m gold in 13:15.29, returning 324 days after Achilles surgery, his seventh European title.

Why these stories are landing together is mostly coincidence of timing rather than a shared cause. The Angels' move follows directly from their record and staff ERA rankings. The FIFA dissent follows from the rejected Forward Enterprise proposal and Johansen's personal history with Infantino. The transfer moves reflect the closing window. The reporting does not tie these threads to one another beyond the calendar.
Desk boards were not available for this edition, so standings, transactions, and injury designations here reflect what is stated directly in today's stories rather than a live league feed.

In the coming days, watch whether the Angels' interim pitching staff shows measurable change before the season's final seven weeks close out, whether Greenard or Stiggers return to practice with the Eagles and Jets, and the outcome of surgery and prognosis for Bardghji. On the FIFA story, watch whether other African federation officials join Johansen or whether CAF's unified backing for Infantino holds. HISA's investigation into the Saratoga and Monmouth Park races should produce post-race drug test results and any formal findings. And the Spence-to-Inter talks remain unresolved, with the fee and timeline still being negotiated.
